verdict.rationale: Semgrep documents writing custom rules for your repositories, describes taint rules as 'simple rules,' and offers an editor and a rule-testing mechanism. Team/Enterprise users can publish private rules to the Registry for use across their organization, and a community user confirms custom rules are readable and practical. Missing for 10: sharing via private Registry rules is limited to the Team/Enterprise tiers, there is no explicit documentation of applying one shared ruleset across multiple repositories, and the pack has no concrete rule-syntax examples.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can write custom static-analysis rules in a simple syntax and share them across repositories

citations.quote: you can write custom rules to determine what Semgrep detects in your repositories
Taint tracking (known also as taint analysis) enables you to write simple rules that catch complex injection bugs
Users with Semgrep Code's Team or Enterprise tier can publish rules to the Semgrep Registry as private rules that are not visible to those outside their organization.
I write custom Semgrep rules to match antipatterns unique to a codebase
